title: Time bound for the pairing machine
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine, let $f$ map Boolean words to Boolean words, and let $T$ map natural numbers to natural numbers. If $M$ computes $f(x)$ within $T(|x|)$ steps for every Boolean input word $x$, then the pairing machine over $M$ computes the function $x\mapsto\langle f(x),x\rangle$ within $4T(n)+2n+8$ steps on inputs of length $n$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Boolean Turing machine
$f$ maps Boolean words to Boolean words
$T$ maps natural numbers to natural numbers
$M$ computes $f$ within time bound $T$ on every input
replaced:
Let the machine $M$ compute a function $f$ within time $T$. Then the pairing
machine over $M$ computes the function $x \mapsto \mathrm{pair}(f(x), x)$ within
time $n \mapsto 4\,T(n) + 2n + 8$: retaining a computed result next to its
original input has a uniform overhead, the capture output length being paid by
the source time.
